arguments.title: First Live Pre-Breach Source-Age Alert — Incident Case Study
arguments.body:
# First Live Pre-Breach Source-Age Alert

## Incident
On August 14, 2025, the qualifying-human-admin source refresh stalled while 17 CS auto-nudge decisions were pending. The source-age alert warned 43 minutes before the freshness limit. Daniela restored the refresh with 18 minutes remaining—before the source crossed its limit.

## Fresh reevaluation
Owen reevaluated all 17 decisions using current source state:
- **13 proceeded.**
- **4 were suppressed** because current Customer Success adoption or renewal work was active.

The warning provided time to restore the source; it did not decide or release any customer action. The governed decision process produced the final outcomes after fresh checks.

## Impact and recovery
No decision became stale. No one manually released a decision, and no rollback or customer correction was required.

## Training takeaway
A pre-breach warning is an opportunity to restore freshness before a fail-closed hold is needed—not permission to bypass fresh evaluation. This first live event is useful operational evidence, but one event does not establish mature reliability or prove that all 17 decisions would otherwise have been incorrect.
